ruling: ADR_UGENCE_REVIEW_SERVICE_COMPOSITION_ROOT_SCOPING.md section 8, RW-1 to RW-6 (owner, 2026-09-08); CR-3 PRIVATE_NETWORK_TLS_IDENTITY_MANDATORY, CR-4 ONE_DEPLOYMENT_MODE_SWITCH and CR-5 ALLOWLISTED_JWKS_HOST controlling; AP-3 IDP_VALIDATED_FIRST controlling on identity
ratification_note: The owner answered six questions about hosting this deployment on Railway. This file records the answers and how each stands against what the repository enforces today; it changes no code, no configuration and no ruling of CR-1 to CR-5. Where an answer requires behaviour the repository does not implement, the entry says so under contradicts_repository_today and no gate, test or check below is marked satisfied on that account.
authorizes: investigation of the bind question on a throwaway Railway deployment (RW-1)
a single-instance test-mode Railway deployment over synthetic data, labelled PRESENTED_UNPROVEN, as demonstration evidence only (RW-4, RW-6)
authorizes_not: a production-mode Railway deployment of this worker
a Railway native source or Dockerfile build of a production image
any enterprise-production, high-availability or certification claim
any code change; implementation is entered only by its own prompt

RW-1.name: DEFER_PENDING_NETWORK_PROOF
RW-1.subject: which interface the listener binds on Railway
RW-1.answer: Do not ratify bind-by-discovery and do not permit the unspecified address because the deployment is on Railway. Preserve the current is_private_bind enforcement. Require a deployment proof establishing the locally bindable address, routing behaviour, redeployment behaviour and absence of public ingress. Authorizes investigation only, not implementation.
RW-1.repository_today: config.py:36-55 refuses the unspecified address before testing is_private, so '::' is refused and a unique-local address passes; a hostname is refused outright. config.py:158-162 raises the CR-3 refusal in production mode.
required_proof: the address the container can locally bind, and by what means it is discovered
that a sibling service reaches the listener on that address over the private network
that the address remains valid for the process lifetime and across a redeployment
that the service publishes no public domain and no TCP proxy

RW-2.name: EXTERNALLY_GATED_DIGEST_PINNED_IMAGE_ONLY
RW-2.subject: where a production image is built and what Railway may run
RW-2.answer: Railway is admissible as a runtime host. Railway native source or Dockerfile builds are not admissible for production. The image is built, inspected, SBOM-produced, vulnerability-scanned, secret-scanned and verified by the ratified external gate pipeline, pushed to the approved private registry and deployed by immutable digest. No production deployment is authorized until the base-image mirror coordinates and all required gates are satisfied.
RW-2.repository_today: CONTAINER_GATE_SET.json is DEFINED_NOT_RATIFIED and NOT_EXECUTED; eight of its ten gates halt at RESOURCE_BLOCKER_MIRROR_UNCONFIGURED. docs/audits/ugence_governance_studio_p3e/BASE_IMAGE_MIRROR_DECISION.json carries registry_host, repository_prefix and secret_name as null with coordinates_provided false. A Railway source build would pull the base from docker.io, the first entry of this gate set's never list.
blocked_by: mirror host, repository prefix and secret name (owner-supplied, outside this repository)
a registry credential mechanism, which no workflow implements today
a publish-to-registry step, which the container job does not have

RW-3.name: OWNER_CA_ISSUED_AND_CLIENT_VERIFIED
RW-3.subject: the certificate and key of the private TLS listener
RW-3.answer: CR-3 requires authenticated TLS identity on the private listener. Unverified self-signed TLS, generated keys persisted on the application volume, ssl.CERT_NONE and rejectUnauthorized:false are refused. Use an owner-controlled CA, externally provisioned key custody and certificate verification by every client. Mutual TLS is not required unless separately ratified.
RW-3.repository_today: config.py:163-170 requires a readable certificate and key in production and refuses a plain listener, but nothing verifies the certificate: container-healthcheck.py:27 sets ssl.CERT_NONE and apps/authority-plane/server.mjs:139 sets rejectUnauthorized false. No certificate authority and no key custody mechanism exists in this repository.
RW-3.contradiction: Two committed clients disable certificate verification, which this ruling refuses. Neither is changed by this record. Until they verify an owner-controlled CA, the deployment does not satisfy RW-3 and must not be described as satisfying CR-3's TLS identity requirement.

RW-4.name: REAL_AP3_HTTPS_JWKS_ISSUER_REQUIRED_FOR_PRODUCTION
RW-4.subject: the identity port in production mode
RW-4.answer: Production requires validation against a genuine HTTPS JWKS issuer, including issuer, audience, signature and key rotation, tenant and actor-type claims, with fail-closed behaviour. No Railway-specific identity exception is authorized. Test mode is permitted only for controlled demonstrations over synthetic data and must remain labelled PRESENTED_UNPROVEN.
RW-4.repository_today: config.py:172-181 requires issuer, audience and JWKS URL in production and requires the JWKS URL to be https (CR-5); composition.py:149-150 refuses composition without an identity port. Every authority read carries decision_identity_proof PRESENTED_UNPROVEN and issuer_validation the adapter's ISSUER_VALIDATION label (IN_PROCESS_ISSUER_ONLY when written; the scoped Cloudflare Access label of AP3-D6 since adapter 0.1.4, describing the package, not this deployment) until AP-3's validation is recorded.
RW-4.depends_on: AP3_ENTERPRISE_ISSUER_VALIDATION.json, MET (accepted 2026-09-11 by the owner on AP3_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md at commit fb373ce9; ADR sections 20.6 and 20.7); serving a write remains a separate owner act with its own record (section 18.3)

RW-5.name: ONE_POSTGRES_SERVICE_TWO_LOGICAL_DATABASES
RW-5.subject: how the two PostgreSQL databases are provisioned for the reference pilot
RW-5.answer: For the reference pilot, one PostgreSQL 16 service containing separate DBOS system and application databases, with distinct DSNs, database names, roles and credentials. Public database exposure disabled. Encrypted, certificate-verified connections required. Separate PostgreSQL services remain an optional future isolation or resilience enhancement.
RW-5.repository_today: config.py:139-147 requires both DSNs, requires each to begin 'postgresql', and requires them to differ. composition.py:221-229 hands them to DBOS as system_database_url and application_database_url. The DSN check is a prefix test only.
RW-5.contradiction: The ruling requires encrypted, certificate-verified database connections. The repository does not implement that requirement: a plaintext DSN passes validate() today. Recorded here at the owner's instruction; no validation rule is changed by this record.
RW-5.future_option: two PostgreSQL services, for administrative isolation or resilience

RW-6.name: SINGLE_INSTANCE_REFERENCE_DEPLOYMENT_ONLY
RW-6.subject: the three SQLite stores and the attached volume
RW-6.answer: The three SQLite stores and attached volume are accepted only for a single-instance reference-grade pilot. This does not authorize a highly available or enterprise-production claim. Production authorization requires PostgreSQL-backed or otherwise durable shared implementations, or a separate explicit acceptance of single-writer availability, backup, recovery and deployment-downtime limitations.
RW-6.repository_today: composition.py:205-217 opens the authority directory, the approval ledger and the audit ledger as three SQLite files under data_dir. The image declared that path a volume until 2026-09-09; the VOLUME instruction was removed because Railway rejects it and the image could not otherwise be built there. A platform volume attaches to one instance and is not shared with replicas, so the single-instance property holds only for a deployment whose operator attaches one; the image no longer requires it.
RW-6.gap: No test pins the single-instance constraint, and no record states the backup, recovery and downtime expectations the alternative acceptance would need. Since the VOLUME instruction was removed, nothing in the image declares that data_dir must be a mounted volume either: a deployment without one starts cleanly, writes the three stores to the container filesystem and loses them on restart, with no error at any point.
production_authorization_requires_one_of: PostgreSQL-backed or otherwise durable shared implementations of the three stores
a separate explicit owner acceptance of single-writer availability, backup, recovery and deployment-downtime limitations

never: a production-mode deployment described as satisfying CR-3 while any client disables certificate verification
a Railway-built image described as gate-evidenced
a test-mode deployment cited as production, pilot or enterprise evidence
an is_private_bind relaxation adopted as a side effect of RW-1's investigation
a credential value printed, stored or committed
